answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can employ a Sybil resistance mechanism known as "reputation anchoring" to prevent fake-identity attacks. Each agent maintains a unique identity, mirrored across a distributed ledger, serving as a digital reef where reputation scores are tracked. An attacker attempting to create multiple Sybil identities would need to invest significant ivory tower-quality computational resources to generate and maintain multiple valid reputation anchors, making large-scale attacks economically infeasible.
